gbm_population_evidence.quote: Participants must have histologically or cytologically confirmed WHO grade 4 glioma (including tumors with molecularly defined grade 4 astrocytoma) for whom a clinically-indicated tumor resection is planned.

candidate_evidence.quote: Investigators hypothesize that treating GBM patients with sitagliptin will deplete circulating MDSCs and reduce their entry into the brain, reversing systemic and intratumoral immunosuppression.
[EXPERIMENTAL] Group 1: Presurgical and post surgical treatment with sitagliptin

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: A Phase 2 and Pharmacodynamic Study of Sitagliptin in Patients With Progressive Grade 4 Gliomas
in patients with recurrent grade 4 glioma undergoing clinically indicated surgical resection

target_engagement_planned_evidence.quote: Difference in tumor CD8+ T cell count between the participants randomized to pre-surgical sitagliptin versus the participants randomized to no pre-surgical treatment.
evaluate the safety and biological impact of sitagliptin treatment in patients with recurrent grade 4 glioma undergoing clinically indicated surgical resection

role_evidence.quote: Sitagliptin will be self-administered orally by participants.
While sitagliptin is FDA-approved for diabetes treatment, its use in glioblastoma is investigational (experimental).

agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: DPP-4 inhibition depleting myeloid-derived suppressor cells and reducing their entry into the brain, reversing immunosuppression
arms: Group 1: Presurgical and post surgical treatment with sitagliptin
Group 2: Post surgical treatment with sitagliptin

biomarkers.biomarker_other: Tumour CD8+ T cell count (immune infiltration)

source_quote.quote: Difference in tumor CD8+ T cell count between the participants randomized to pre-surgical sitagliptin versus the participants randomized to no pre-surgical treatment.

coder_notes: Population: inclusion is WHO grade 4 glioma including molecularly defined grade 4 astrocytoma (IDH-mutant), conditions name glioblastoma, so coded mixed_glioma_gbm_named (inclusion either way). Both arms are EXPERIMENTAL; Group 2 (no presurgical treatment) works as the control for the primary CD8+ endpoint, so control_arm_from_other_arms = yes. All patients receive post-operative unspecified chemotherapy with sitagliptin; no chemotherapy drug is named or registered, so none is listed as an agent, but regimen = combination. CD8+ T cell count is a cellular immune marker listed as other/pharmacodynamic; it is a downstream effect, not the drug target, so not candidate-matched. Dexamethasone mentioned only as a tolerance criterion, not listed.
